abstraction_design.rationale: Leaf abstractions (card, refs-to-species, formatters) stretch nicely, but the route-level page shape was never abstracted, so a similar-but-different section like Items is mostly a copy of an existing route.

findings.issue: The typeNames Map→Object.fromEntries→new Map(Object.entries()) round-trip is repeated in all five routes (10 occurrences), so any change to how type labels flow touches every route file.
findings.suggestion: Pass a serializable [{name,label}] array from a single data helper (or add serialize/hydrate helpers in lib) so routes stop hand-rolling the dance.

findings.issue: The detail-page shape (handler fetch + 404 handling + facts dl + effect section + learned-by card grid) is duplicated across moves, abilities and types routes with only wording differing; a new Items page would copy ~140 lines.
findings.suggestion: Extract shared fragments in views.js (e.g. a facts-dl builder and a standard notFound props/status helper) so new resource pages become configuration plus small templates.

findings.issue: Pokémon card ordering is decided in two places (species list sort at data.js:46 and refs sort at data.js:73), so a global order change (e.g. sort by name) must be found and applied twice.
findings.suggestion: Centralize card ordering in one helper or accept an explicit comparator from callers.

findings.issue: pokemonCard only receives {speciesId, speciesName}, so a sprite fix that needs the default Pokémon's actual sprites.front_default would require plumbing fetched data through three call sites (views.js, data.js:52, index.js) instead of one.
findings.suggestion: Have pokemonRefsToSpecies carry the default Pokémon's sprite URL it already fetched, and let pokemonCard accept an optional spriteUrl override.

findings.issue: The fetch→DOMParser→replaceWith refresh routine is duplicated in pokemon/[name].client.js with only the target id differing.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared swapFragment(url, elementId) helper into src/lib and import it from both client scripts.

findings.issue: The option() helper is defined identically in index.js:17.
The 404 flow (responseInit.status + {notFound:true} + template guard) is repeated in four routes.
findings.suggestion: Add a small notFoundProps() helper next to notFoundContent in views.js.

findings.issue: .ability-list and .evolution-tree share selector lists, so removing the Abilities feature means editing combined selectors rather than deleting a block.
findings.suggestion: Give each feature its own rules or a clearly labeled shared 'tree list' class.

summary: A tidy, idiomatic Gracile 0.11 app with the right low-level seams: one card component, one refs-to-species resolver, one API/cache module, and clean server/client separation. Editability holds up well for leaf-level changes (sprite, card content, styling) but weakens at the route level, where the detail-page shape, 404 flow and typeNames plumbing are duplicated across moves/abilities/types. Scored 4 overall: easy to change in place, slightly copy-prone to extend.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete one route file; then remove the Abilities section in the Pokémon page template (:291-302) and its handler mapping (:197-204); CSS needs an edit because .ability-list shares selectors with .evolution-tree. No nav link, no data-layer references.

scenarios.change: Fix wrong sprite for species whose default Pokémon differs (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: If it's a URL-pattern issue, views.js:6 spriteUrl is the only place — trivial. But the correct data-driven fix (use the default Pokémon's front_default) requires pokemonCard to accept a sprite, pokemonRefsToSpecies (which already fetches each Pokémon, data.js:52) to carry it, and the home page to gain a per-species fetch path — three coordinated files, though every list shares the one card markup so no list is missed.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: All four lists get their order from two spots in data.js (:46 species list, :73 refs resolver), so a server-side order change is two lines in one file — but it's implicit knowledge; nothing documents that card ordering lives there, and a per-page sort would instead touch every route.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: The lib layer (api, pokemonRefsToSpecies, pokemonCard, cardList, util, document) is fully reusable — reuse is real. Mechanical, but it cements the duplication.

scenarios.notes: Base URL construction (api.js:5-8), the /api/v2/ path prefix and both cache sites live in one 60-line module; views.js's spriteUrl reuses apiBase rather than re-hardcoding the host. Only nit: the promise-cache miss pattern is written twice within that file (api() and apiList()).
